national_raw_news.content: Parliament has passed the National Co-operative Development Corporation(NCDC) (Amendment) Bill, 2026 with Rajya Sabha approving it today. Lok Sabha has already passed the Bill. Minister of State for Cooperation Murlidhar Mohol moved the bill, which aims to further amend the National Co-operative Development Corporation Act, 1962. The Bill allows the Corporation to undertake its activities in industrial goods. The legislation also allows the state governments to extend funding from the Corporation to any entity engaged in co-operative development. The Corporation can also provide loans and grants directly to any co-operative society or entity engaged in co-operative development. Replying to discussion, Mr Mohol said that through this Bill, the welfare and economic empowerment of crores of farmers across the country will be strengthened. He noted that NCDC, was established to provide financial assistance for the organised and sustained development of the cooperative sector in the country. The Minister highlighted that from the establishment of NCDC in 1963 until 2014, the previous government provided financial assistance of only around 45 thousand crore rupees. He, however, said, in the last 12 years since 2014, financial assistance has increased to around four lakh crore rupees. The Minister highlighted that India’s cooperative sector is among the largest cooperative networks in the world. Mr Mohol said that today, the country has more than eight lakh cooperative societies, with around 30 crore members associated with them. He informed that 80 thousand Primary Agricultural Credit Societies, PACS, are being computerised and have been enabled to undertake around 25 different types of business activities. The Minister informed that Tribhuvan Sahkari University has been established to provide trained and skilled manpower to the cooperative sector. Mr Mohol said that through this institution, around 17 lakh young people will be trained over the next five years and will contribute to the cooperative sector. He said, more than 163 major initiatives have been undertaken in the cooperative sector in just last five years.

national_raw_news.title: 59 mins ago | National 38 Opposition shying away from discussion on NEET paper leak issue, says Parliamentary Affairs Minis...
national_raw_news.content: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said that Home Minister Amit Shah wrote a letter to the Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla stating once again that he is open to having a detailed discussion on the several incidents that took place during the protest on NEET paper leak issue. Talking to reporters in the Parliament complex, the Minister said, the government itself is saying that it is ready for a discussion and will provide answers, but the Opposition does not want to hear the answers and is shying away from the discussion. Mr Rijiju said that he is deeply saddened as the opposition members of Parliament are not allowing Parliament to function properly.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | Sports 289 Commonwealth Fencing: India get 3 gold, one silver and one bronze across various individual events
national_raw_news.content: The Indian fencing team collected three gold, one silver, and one bronze medal across various senior individual events on the third day of the Commonwealth Championship at Lagos in Nigeria today. Team India’s stellar day three performance brought the nation’s overall combined medal count to an extraordinary 29 medals, comprising 8 Gold, 7 Silver, and 14 Bronze. India established immediate dominance in the Senior Women’s Foil category, securing a gold-silver victory. Kanaglakshmi captured the gold medal following a precise and controlled campaign, while teammate Joys Ashitha took silver to claim the top two spots on the podium ahead of England’s Georgia Green and Emily Goodchild, who won Bronze. The success continued in the Senior Men’s Epee discipline, where Rajendran Shanthimol Sherjin put on a commanding display to secure country’s second gold medal of the day. Sherjin outpointed South Africa’s Kruger Pieter, who finished with silver, while Wales’ Burkhardt Marc and South Africa’s Losevsky Sergey shared the bronze medals. In the Senior Men’s Sabre event, Singh Karan Singh clinched India’s third gold medal of the day with an outstanding final fight against Australia’s Shim Yoongi, who took silver. Teammate Kumaresan Padma Gisho Nidhi added to the medal haul by winning bronze alongside Nigeria’s Akinyosoye Oluwafolayemi.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | Business 79 India’s $30 Trillion Economy Vision by 2047 provides major Opportunities for Businesses: Commerce...
national_raw_news.content: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has urged Indian businesses and citizens to adopt fair trading practices, promote recycling and reuse, and encourage a circular economy while taking Indian products and services to global markets. The Minister said this while addressing the inaugural ceremony of Bharatiya Vyapari Mahotsav 2026 in New Delhi today. He said that India’s current economic size of around four trillion dollars presents a major opportunity as the country moves towards the vision of becoming a thirty trillion dollar economy by the year 2047. Highlighting the government’s trade initiatives, the minister said that free trade agreements signed over the last four years cover 38 developed nations with a combined GDP of 60 trillion dollars. He added that that markets have been opened for Indian industry and businesses through nine free trade agreements. The Minister emphasized that India’s goods and services exports reached a record level of 863 trillion dollars last year, comprising 442 trillion dollars of merchandise exports and 421 trillion dollars of services exports. He noted that the exports had registered around 73 per cent growth over the last six years and that the target for the current year is to achieve exports of one trillion dollars. Talking about the event, the Minister said that the vision of Bharatiya Vyapar Mahotsav is to showcase India’s growing prowess across sectors, including space technology and defence, to fuel the country’s progress towards Atmanirbhar Bharat. Speaking on the occasion, Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada said that technology and trade are twin engines of India’s growth story. The Minister highlighted that Free Trade Agreements signed under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi with 27 developed nations, including the European Union, are a matter of pride for the country. He said developed nations today see India as a ray of hope. The Minister called on businesses and traders to work together with those of FTA countries to derive the benefit of such agreements. The Bharatiya Vyapar Mahotsav 2026 is a vibrant celebration of Made in India, Made for India, Made for the World. The four-day exhibition will demonstrate the country’s trade strength, economic confidence, entrepreneurial spirit and unwavering resolve towards an Atmanirbhar Bharat. It is jointly organised by the Confederation of All India Traders and the India Trade Promotion Organisation in New Delhi.

national_raw_news.title: 4 hours ago | National 88 Lok Sabha referred FCRA to JPC for further scrutiny
national_raw_news.content: Lok Sabha today referred the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, to the Joint Parliamentary Committee for further scrutiny. The bill aims to further amend the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010. The objective of the Bill is to make the use of foreign contributions more transparent and accountable. Minister of State for Home Nityanand Rai moved the Bill to refer it to JPC comprising members of both the Houses for wider consultations. He said, the committee will consist of 21 members from the Lok Sabha, nominated by the Speaker, and 10 members from the Rajya Sabha, nominated by the Chairman. Mr Rai said, the Committee will submit its report to this House by the last day of the first week of the winter session.

national_raw_news.title: Vriksh Mitra Parivar Drives Nationwide Plantation Campaign Under PM Modi’s ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ Call
national_raw_news.content: More than 50,000 saplings were planted across the country on the occasion of Hariyali Amavasya. This is a part of a nationwide plantation drive led by Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shivraj Singh Chouhan in collaboration with the Vriksh Mitra Parivar. The campaign drew further momentum from Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative. The programme was organised today in New Delhi. Speaking on the occasion Mr Chouhan said Hariyali Amavasya is not only a religious occasion but also an opportunity to express gratitude towards nature. The Minister urged every citizen to plant at least one tree each year and encourage five others to join the campaign. Mr Chouhan also called upon panchayats, urban local bodies and institutions to identify designated areas for plantation so that saplings can be protected and maintained over the long term. Highlighting the close link between environmental sustainability and agriculture, the Minister said environmental degradation directly affects farming, water availability, soil health and human well-being.

national_raw_news.title: One Herb, One Standard initiative aims to protect India’s traditional medicine heritage, says AYUSH Minister
national_raw_news.content: AYUSH Minister Prataprao Jadhav today said that One Herb, One Standard initiative aims to strengthen the quality and credibility of Traditional Medicines. Mr Jadhav was addressing the event on the renewal of Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the implementation of the One Herb, One Standard initiative today. The Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy, Ministry of Ayush, and the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission, renewed the MoU. Addressing the event, the Minister said, the initiative will contribute to protecting India’s rich biodiversity and traditional medicine heritage, while strengthening India’s position as a trusted global standard-setter in medicinal plants, traditional medicines and their quality standards. He said, harmonised standards would help address potential confusion among stakeholders and establish a stronger and coordinated framework for the standardisation of medicinal plants. Ayush Ministry said that the renewed MoU will continue the inter-ministerial cooperation for a further period of three years, with the objective of developing uniform, reliable and scientifically robust quality standards for single drugs of plant origin used across Ayurveda, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa, Unani and Homoeopathy systems of medicine.

national_raw_news.title: Railways approves Kavach Version 4.0 at estimated cost of 295 crore rupees
national_raw_news.content: Indian Railways has approved the provision of Kavach Version 4.0 on 660 route Kilometer of the Izzatnagar Division of North Eastern Railway at an estimated cost of 295 crore rupees. The Ministry of Railways informed that Kavach Version 4.0 has been approved under the umbrella work Provision of Kavach with communication backbone of Long-Term Evolution on balance sections of Indian Railways. It added that the approved work covers the balance sections of the Izzatnagar Division of North Eastern Railway. The provision of Kavach Version 4.0 will further strengthen the safety infrastructure on the identified railway sections. Kavach is India’s indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection system designed to prevent Signal Passed at Danger incidents and train collisions through continuous monitoring of train movements. The system automatically applies brakes whenever required, enables trains to safely operate at maximum permissible speeds, improves operational reliability and supports safe train operations even during adverse weather conditions such as dense fog.

national_raw_news.title: Thailand: Education Ministry plans to elevate schools’ safety after fatal shooting
national_raw_news.content: Thailand’s cabinet has approved an Education Ministry’s proposal to elevate school safety to a national agenda, following a mass shooting at a secondary school outside Bangkok last week that killed nine people. Deputy government spokesperson Patdarasm Thongsaluaykorn said, the move aims to strengthen prevention and response at educational institutions systematically, protecting children, teachers and education personnel nationwide. Under a ministry announcement effective immediately, Ms Patdarasm said all schools have been designated School Safety Zones and must set up centres for the protection of rights, liberties and safety on their premises. In a statement, she said the core of the approach is preventing risk before an incident occurs through strict searches and screening for weapons, illegal items and dangerous objects before entry, alongside mental health support systems covering both the physical and psychological welfare of students, teachers and staff.

national_raw_news.title: Philippine facing risk of waterborne diseases after floods
national_raw_news.content: Philippine health authorities have issued an alert on water-borne diseases after floods hit the northern part of the country. The local health centre in the Ilocos region has warned residents of rising health risks as enhanced southwest monsoon rains continue to trigger flooding across the region. Residents were urged to guard against water-borne illnesses such as influenza, leptospirosis and dengue, which commonly spread during the rainy season. Red and yellow alerts were raised for power grids in central and southern Philippines today as several power plants remained unavailable. The Philippine National Police (PNP) has intensified post-disaster recovery efforts in the wake of tropical cyclones Luis and Maymay and the enhanced southwest monsoon. The PNP reported 26 weather-related fatalities till yesterday, including 25 civilians and one police officer.

national_raw_news.title: Sports Ministry suspends TTFI’s recognition till restoration of its governance structure 3 hours ago 34
national_raw_news.content: The Sports Ministry today suspended its recognition of the Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI)and asked the Indian Olympic Association to form an ad-hoc committee to administer the sport, citing governance deficiencies within TTFI. In its order, the Ministry cited TTFI’s failure to conduct elections on time as one of the reasons for the suspension after getting an unsatisfactory response to a show cause notice issued earlier. The Ministry stated that the IOA, in consultation with the international body (ITTF) will take appropriate action to create an internal regulatory mechanism, including the constitution of an ad-hoc committee, till such time that a duly constituted governance structure is restored in TTFI.

national_raw_news.title: Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa defeats Javokhir Sindarov in Sinquefield Cup 5 hours ago 166
national_raw_news.content: Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa defeated Javokhir Sindarov in a second-round match of the Sinquefield Cup in St Louis, United States. It is his first victory in the tournament, which is the penultimate event of the Grand Chess Tour. Praggnanandhaa dominated the game from start to finish. He slowly pressed his advantage in the endgame, which arose from a queen pawn opening. Sindarov chose an endgame that was equal and should have ended in a draw. But he could not match Praggnanandhaa’s determination. The Indian kept pressing and eventually turned the drawn position into a winning one. The game lasted 95 moves. With this victory, Praggnanandhaa moved to 1.5 points from two games.

national_raw_news.title: BRICS economies are major growth engines of global economy, says FM Sitharaman 20 seconds ago
national_raw_news.content: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that public capital should act as a catalyst for private investment, rather than a substitute for it. Addressing a seminar in Jaipur on the role of the New Development Bank in mobilising private capital in BRICS member countries, Mrs. Sitharaman said BRICS economies are among the major engines of global growth, but they also face challenges in attracting private capital. She said that besides ensuring the availability of capital, it is equally important to build investor confidence, maintain stability and provide a predictable, long-term policy framework. The Finance Minister highlighted the role of multilateral development banks in reducing investment risks, making projects more financially viable and strengthening investor confidence, thereby helping mobilise private capital on a larger scale. Referring to India’s experience, Mrs. Sitharaman said the Central Government has strengthened the country’s infrastructure through sustained public capital expenditure and structural reforms. New Development Bank President Dilma Rousseff also addressed the seminar. Earlier, Economic Affairs Secretary Anuradha Thakur said that increasing private capital participation is an important need in the current economic environment. The seminar is being held as part of the BRICS Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors’ meeting in Jaipur under India’s BRICS Chairship 2026, with the objective of strengthening cooperation on global economic and financial issues.

national_raw_news.title: India’s retail inflation rises to 4.45%, remains above RBI’s target of 4% 1 hour ago 878
national_raw_news.content: India’s retail inflation accelerated to 4.45 per cent on an annual basis in July, remaining above the Reserve Bank of India’s target of 4 per cent for the second consecutive month this year. The July inflation reading was moderately higher than the 4.38 per cent recorded in June as food prices remained elevated. The current print is the highest reading under the new 2024-base year Consumer Price Index (CPI) series. According to data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, inflation in rural areas increased to 4.84 per cent, while in urban regions it rose to 3.96 per cent. The food inflation rate, based on the All India Consumer Food Price Index, stood at 5.52 per cent last month, up from 5.32 per cent in the preceding month. According to the data, the increase in inflation in July was mainly attributed to rising prices in personal care, social protection, restaurants and accommodation services, food and beverages and intoxicants. The top items showing high inflation at the all India combined level included Silver, Gold, Diamond and Platinum Jewellery, Ginger, Garlic and Onion. In contrast, items with lowest inflation included Potato, Motor Car and Jeep, Lady’s finger, Peas, and Tomato.
